rationales: There are not eight possible combinations of solute and solvent states.
There are nine types of solution based on the physical states of solute and solvent.
Seven is not the number of possible physical-state combinations.
There are not ten possible combinations of solute and solvent states.
Oxygen is a pure substance, not a solution.
Carbon dioxide is a pure compound, not a solution.
Air is a homogeneous mixture of gases and is a solution.
Nitrogen is a pure substance, not a solution.
HF is formed by sharing electrons, not by electron transfer.
The shared electrons are unequally attracted, so the bond is not non-polar.
HF does not form its bond by coordinate donation of an electron pair.
HF has a polar covalent bond because fluorine attracts the shared electrons more strongly.
Donation of electrons alone describes neither covalent bond formation nor its defining feature.
Acceptance of electrons alone does not describe covalent bond formation.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electrons.
Repulsion of electrons does not form a covalent bond.
Alkali metals are Group 1 elements, not d-block elements.
Halogens are Group 17 elements, not d-block elements.
d-block elements are commonly called transition metals.
Alkaline earth metals are Group 2 elements, not d-block elements.
Rutherford proposed a nuclear model but did not introduce quantized orbits.
Planck introduced the quantum concept, not the atomic orbit model.
Bohr used the concept of fixed orbits for electrons in his atomic model.
J.J. Thomson proposed the plum-pudding model, not the orbit model.
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt.
CaC₂ is calcium carbide, not common salt.
SiO₂ is silicon dioxide, not common salt.
CaO is calcium oxide, not common salt.
Sulphur is generally dull, not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Carbon is not the standard example of a lustrous non-metal in this context.
Ether is not commonly called the universal solvent.
Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves many substances.
Sodium carbonate is a compound, not a universal solvent.
Sulphur is not a solvent and is insoluble in water.
Alcohol mixes with water.
Sugar dissolves in water.
Sodium carbonate dissolves in water.

15.2°C is higher than the accepted transition temperature of tin.

Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among these halogens.

C₂H₂ contains a carbon–carbon triple covalent bond.
